tagline: Northwest out of Flagstaff, around the shoulder of Arizona's highest mountain.
intro: US 180 leaves Flagstaff heading northwest along the flank of the San Francisco Peaks, the remnant of a single larger volcano. Humphreys Peak, the highest point in the state, stands at 12,633 feet. The road runs through the pine forest, aspen groves and open prairie of the Coconino National Forest.

Snowbowl sits on the western slopes of Humphreys Peak. The Forest Service allowed a road and ski lodge there in 1938, twenty-three years after Ole and Pete Solberg first came down Flagstaff's Mars Hill on homemade wooden skis.

moments.title: Museum of Northern Arizona
moments.text: A zoologist and an artist from Philadelphia founded it in 1928 in two rooms of the Flagstaff Woman's Club. One curator stayed 51 years.

moments.title: Fort Valley
moments.text: Settled in 1881 at the foot of Mount Agassiz and named for a fort built against the Apache that was never actually used.

moments.title: Lava River Cave
moments.text: Three quarters of a mile of lava tube, found by lumbermen in 1915. It holds near 40 degrees all summer, often with ice on some of the rocks.
